assumptions: Stock Radicle issue and patch semantics suffice for the full methodology lifecycle without custom COBs; this is the migration program's inhabit-first premise, validated by lived use after implementation — not proven by this survey.

Contributor-authority coverage holds as documented: any peer can open issues, comment, and publish patch revisions ('anyone can do that' per the current user guide); the exact permission matrix for issue assignment and labeling by non-delegates is not fully documented (UNCONFIRMED) — if assignment proves delegate-only, the claim mechanic falls back to the comment convention already anticipated by the work-unit lifecycle requirement.

The connector-era milestone will be accepted without changes that move the surveyed seam: 76 unreleased commits exist post-rc.1 and none observed touch the capability contract, but the seam must be re-checked cheaply when the release gate is crossed.

A Radicle node can run persistently enough on the operator's key-holding device — and/or a project-controlled always-on seed — for agent-authored state to replicate and be verified; no such node or seed exists today.

rad's ssh-agent integration behaves as documented on the delegate device (OpenSSH >= 9.1, agent-based signing); ssh-agent socket forwarding into other execution contexts is officially UNCONFIRMED and the chosen per-session-identity topology deliberately avoids depending on it.

The documented Radicle 1.9.x command surface (radicle.dev guides and man pages, verified 2026-07-10) matches the binaries that will be installed; because rad is absent on-device today, the first implementation act re-verifies the actual installed command surface before mechanics are frozen.

The operator accepts per-session/per-agent Radicle identities as the agent execution model (mirroring agentd's existing per-agent SSH identity pattern, but with keys generated inside the session boundary rather than mounted into it).
constraints: Stock Radicle only, as it presently ships (1.9.x surface): built-in issues and patches treated as native user-facing facilities; no custom COB types, reducers, action schemas, or namespaces (rad cob create/update for external types exists but is out of bounds this phase); no dependency on the WeForge MVP existing.

Release gate: implementation must not begin before the connector-based Tesserine milestone is accepted, integrated, tagged, and published — concretely, M1 integration verification (commons#50) accepted and the final connector-era releases cut from the current RC lines (groundwork v0.3.0-rc.1 -> v0.3.0; runa v0.2.0-rc.1 -> v0.2.0). Survey and decomposition may precede publication; destabilizing the release-candidate line is prohibited.

Decision authority: commons owns FORGE-CAPABILITY.md and ADR-0016/0017; retirement of forge neutrality lands as the commons Radicle-substrate ADR (commons#108, gated on commons#50). Groundwork implements that decision in its own substrate and does not unilaterally rewrite commons artifacts.

runa is consumed as-is at its methodology interface (artifact types, protocol declarations, trigger conditions): the replacement must run on a runa project with no [forge] section — verified optional end-to-end at runa 0.2.0-rc.1 — and any runa engine change is a named dependency, never a silent assumption.

Every durable Radicle mutation is signed by construction and there is no unauthenticated mutation path (radicle-httpd is read-only); the workflow design therefore cannot route around identity custody, and the identity topology is a load-bearing part of the replacement, not an ops afterthought.
ADR-0017's identity discipline — complete, scoped identity validated before any operation — remains binding for Radicle handles (RID-scoped COB OIDs).

The current agent execution boundary cannot run Radicle: rad is absent from the babbie host, the tesserine/base session image, and agentd; the runner accepts only https/ssh/git repo URL forms and its existing credential seams copy key material into containers. Radicle-native operation at that boundary is enabled by external work in base/agentd/babbie-ops and must not be worked around by weakening the custody mandate.
ADR-0009's runtime-state policy continues to govern: .runa/workspace/ is committed durable project state; store/config/state remain machine-local regardless of substrate.

The canonical repository homes remain where they are (GitHub) during this work: rad-initialized Radicle homes carry the live collaboration lifecycle, while the existing origins persist as historical record until the later, out-of-scope canonical transfer; retaining a plain git remote is not 'GitHub as a supported backend' — no connector operations against it remain.
dependencies: commons#50 — M1 integration verification accepted: the gate for publishing the connector-era milestone.
Final connector-era releases tagged and published: groundwork v0.3.0 and runa v0.2.0 — the final stable baseline of the connector era that must exist before this replacement begins.

commons#108 — the 'Radicle as the native collaboration substrate' ADR (blocked on commons#50): the constitutional decision this replacement implements; groundwork#538 is the roadmap stub for this body of work and must be re-scoped to this requirements' stock-substrate boundary (its current custom-COB framing is superseded by the operator intent).

Radicle enablement at the execution boundary (external repos: base, agentd, babbie-ops): rad 1.9.x and a node on the operator device; per-agent RAD_HOME/identity provisioning inside session containers without ever mounting the operator key; runner acceptance of Radicle-sourced working copies (repo_url_kind currently rejects rad://); seeding policy for agent-authored state. Groundwork's substrate change can be authored and conformance-tested before this completes, but end-to-end removal evidence depends on it.
rad-initialization and seeding of the working repositories (beginning with tesserine/groundwork itself) under the operator's delegate identity.

Optional, non-blocking runa/agentd follow-ups, named so decomposition does not silently absorb them: extending runa's intent.target promised-entry grammar to Radicle issue references; retiring runa-forge-* crates, [forge] config, RUNA_FORGE_* atoms, and agentd's GROUNDWORK_FORGE_TYPE (their own exigencies, already aligned with the runa#226 retirement direction).
commons cleanup of FORGE-CAPABILITY.md and supersession notices on ADR-0016/0017 — external and non-blocking for Groundwork's in-repo replacement.
functional_requirements: Work-unit lifecycle on native Radicle issues: decompose opens work-units as issues (rad issue open --title --description --label), acquisition reads them including the comment log (rad issue show), progress is recorded as issue comments (rad issue comment), claiming is reflected by DID assignment (rad issue assign --add <did>) or by a documented comment convention if non-delegate assignment proves unavailable, and close-out records completion context as a comment plus a state transition (rad issue state --solved, or --closed with reason) — replacing read-work-unit, create-work-unit, claim-work-unit, record-progress, and close-out.

Work-unit identity re-homed: the opaque {id, display} handle shape is retained, but its semantics move from commons FORGE-CAPABILITY.md to a Groundwork-owned Radicle identity definition — a complete, scoped identity naming the repository (RID) and the issue COB OID, honoring ADR-0017's completeness-and-scope discipline; the acquisition state vocabulary (materialize.py CLOSED_STATES, currently GitHub 'closed' / SourceHut 'resolved') becomes Radicle's open/closed/solved.

Change submission through native patches: submit delivers a change-proposal by pushing the prepared commit to Radicle's magic ref (git push rad <commit>:refs/patches, with -o patch.message for deterministic titling); the change-proposal artifact binds the patch COB OID in its handle and binds each immutable submission round (version) to the specific patch revision OID it delivered, so review and land bind to (patch, revision), never to a mutable branch tip; revision rounds are published as new immutable patch revisions by pushing the revised commit to the patch upstream (rad/patches/<id>).

Review operates on the delivered patch: the reviewer inspects via rad patch show / rad patch diff (revision base..head ranges support git range-diff); the typed disposition artifacts (change-approved, change-needs-revision) remain the methodology's judgment record; reflecting the disposition onto the collaboration substrate is a native patch review (rad patch review --accept | --reject --message, addressed to the reviewed revision) — replacing reflect-disposition.

Landing through ordinary Git merge mechanics: land applies the approved revision by merging the approved commit into the canonical default branch and publishing with git push rad <branch>; Radicle marks the patch merged and updates the canonical head automatically on that push; completion-record.merge_reference records the resulting canonical head / merge commit SHA; close-out then completes on the corresponding issue — replacing apply-approved-change.

Durable-mutation verification as first-class mechanics: every required Git or Radicle mutation is verified by reading back resulting durable state — rad issue show for issue mutations; rad patch show (state, revisions, reviews, merged) for patch mutations; canonical-head / git ls-remote rad confirmation for branch publication; rad sync status and push sync reporting for replication — under an explicit replication policy naming which nodes must hold the state (minimum-replica / preferred-seed semantics of rad sync). A refused, failed, or unpropagated mutation fails the protocol; local COB or ref creation alone never satisfies a durable-mutation criterion.

Mechanics re-homing: the git/rad invocations become Groundwork-owned mechanics referenced by the C-2 workflow contracts and protocol prose exactly where the eight operations are invoked today (submit.toml, land.toml, decompose/acquire/define prose); the forge-operation registry injection (tooling/workflow_contracts.py merging capability operation names into the mechanic registry) is deleted, dissolving the forge/non-forge mechanic split so all mechanics are ordinary runtime actions.

Deletion surface executed and replaced where invariants remain: remove schemas/forge-capability/v2 and tooling/forge_capability.py; remove the capability-contract, artifact-handle-drift, exactly-eight, and forge-leakage conformance gates in tooling/conformance.py, replacing them with Radicle-era gates protecting the new invariants (handle grammar, mechanics registry integrity, absence of connector-era surfaces); retire test_forge_capability.py's connector-model assertions, provider-named fixtures, stale retired-era mechanic fixtures and orphaned .pyc residue; update README, connecting-structure, schemas/README, work-unit-craft, and acquire prose that document the connector model; installer output carries no adapter-era surfaces.

Decision record and documentation: a Groundwork ADR records the substrate replacement and supersedes ADR-0002's forge-capability layer, tracing to the commons Radicle-substrate ADR once landed; user-facing documentation describes the git+rad workflow and its prerequisites (rad CLI, node, identity, seeding) in place of connector and PAT configuration; the CHANGELOG carries the user-visible surface change.

Freshen/graph facets re-derived from the real substrate: freshen-record's tracker-graph facets (blockers, blocked, epic_membership, siblings, milestone, labels) are re-specified against what stock Radicle issues actually provide — labels and DID assignees exist; milestones and native issue relations do not. Each facet either receives a Radicle-native derivation (labels, body/comment conventions) or is deliberately retired with recorded rationale; GitHub tracker concepts are not reproduced by convention for their own sake.

Cold-start acquisition from a Radicle issue: the acquire path materializes a work-unit artifact from an existing rad issue reference (RID plus issue OID); until runa's intent.target promised-entry grammar (currently GitHub/SourceHut forms only) is extended, acquisition remains reachable through an intent statement carrying the issue identity, without connector mediation.

Identity topology for the smallest secure execution boundary, using stock Radicle's one-DID-per-device model: the operator's Radicle identity — the repository delegate — remains on the physical device where it was created; agent sessions operate as their own per-session or per-agent Radicle identities created inside the session boundary, holding contributor authority only (open issues, comment, push to their own namespaces, open patches and publish revisions — capabilities stock Radicle grants any peer). Canonical acts (canonical-branch publication, identity-document changes, delegate-gated operations) execute only where delegate authority lives: on the operator's device, or through canonical-reference rules (payload.xyz.radicle.crefs allow lists, which may name non-delegate DIDs per ref pattern) granting a specific session identity exactly the refs it needs. No private key is copied into repositories, containers, environment variables, secret stores, prompts, or agent workspaces; RAD_PASSPHRASE-in-environment is prohibited as a custody mechanism.

Propagation topology defined and enforced: agent-session-authored state must verifiably reach the canonical node(s) — the workflow declares which node(s) seed the working repositories and with what scope (followed vs all) so that per-session DIDs' issues and patches replicate, and the verification mechanics check against that declared policy.

Removal evidence: completion of this body of work is demonstrated by (a) a conformance/test gate asserting absence of the connector-era surfaces (no vendored capability schema, no forge-operation names in the mechanic registry, no connector-model documentation obligations), (b) the full methodology lifecycle exercised end-to-end on stock Radicle with recorded durable-state evidence for every mutation class (issue open/comment/assign/close; patch open/revise/review/merge; canonical publication; replication readback), and (c) Groundwork operating on a runa project with no [forge] configuration.
non_functional_requirements: Grounded completion: no protocol reports success on command invocation or local artifact production; completion claims are grounded in read-back durable Git/Radicle state, and the verify station's existing evidence discipline (execution-binding stamps per policy.toml) applies unchanged to the new mechanics.

Key custody: the delegate private signing identity never leaves its device; agent sessions hold at most their own bounded contributor identities, so the blast radius of a compromised session is that session's DID — never the repository's canonical authority.

Single canonical path: after the arc, exactly one collaboration implementation exists — no dynamic dispatch, no dormant connector path, no compatibility architecture intended to outlive the replacement.

One coherent, reviewable replacement: a single governing architectural objective carried through to complete removal of the superseded system, executed as reviewable commits with mechanical checks and recoverable checkpoints; conformance and release ceremony stay green throughout the arc.

Sovereignty preserved: protocols and work-unit records continue to pass outcomes, not procedure; the new mechanics are HOW-recipes referenced from workflow contracts, and the methodology semantics (work, proposal, review, revision, approval, application, disposition, closure, verifiable completion) keep their existing artifact homes.

Simplicity discipline: no speculative abstraction over rad/git; any new module, schema, or tool boundary must be justified by actual ownership, testability, or the security boundary — otherwise protocol prose plus mechanics suffice.
scope:
Territory: the Groundwork methodology repository (tesserine/groundwork @ 0f1fdd4, v0.3.0-rc.1 plus 76 unreleased commits) and the seams it actually collaborates through: the vendored commons Forge Capability v2 contract, the runa 0.2.0-rc.1 runtime whose MCP surface serves the eight connector operations, and the agentd/base/babbie execution boundary where agent sessions run in one-shot podman containers. Surveyed against the operator's decided direction — remove forge polymorphism and realize Groundwork's durable collaboration mechanics directly in ordinary Git plus stock Radicle — with Radicle 1.9.1 (current stable) grounded in the official radicle.dev guides and man pages; the rad toolchain is installed nowhere on this host today.

Descriptive state, grounded: Groundwork's per-provider connector code is already retired in-repo. What remains of forge polymorphism inside Groundwork is one contract and its enforcement: schemas/forge-capability/v2 (vendored, commons-authored, exactly eight operations over opaque {id, display} handles), its loader tooling/forge_capability.py, the registry injection at tooling/workflow_contracts.py:79-80 that lets workflow contracts name forge operations as mechanics (submit.toml: deliver-change-proposal; land.toml: apply-approved-change, reflect-disposition, close-out), protocol and skill prose invoking create-work-unit (decompose), read-work-unit (acquire, define), claim-work-unit (define workspace), and record-progress, conformance gates that actively police the connector model (capability provenance pin, exactly-eight-operations, forge-leakage token scan, retired-asset checks), test_forge_capability.py with provider-named fixtures plus stale retired-era residue, installer and README/ADR documentation of the adapter surface, and freshen-record's six tracker-graph facets that encode GitHub-era tracker concepts. Provider registration, active-forge selection, dispatch, and PAT injection live in runa (runa-forge-github, runa-forge-sourcehut, runa-forge-compose behind optional [forge] config) — and runa's methodology interface carries no forge primitive at all: a methodology that names no connector operations runs on today's runa unchanged, with no [forge] section. review.toml and verify.toml already invoke zero forge operations. The judgment this grounds: the actual architectural seam being removed from Groundwork is the vendored capability contract plus its eight invocation points and the conformance, test, documentation, and identity surfaces that hold it in place — not a connector registry, which Groundwork does not contain; the registry's removal is runa's own exigence.

Normative need: the methodology's durable collaboration semantics — work, proposal, review, revision, approval, application, disposition, closure, verifiable completion — must survive with one direct realization on the substrate that natively provides repository identity, signed authorship, issues, patches, revisions, and synchronization. Stock Radicle provides exactly these as Git mechanics plus a small rad command set, all mutations signed by construction (the HTTP daemon is read-only, so no unauthenticated mutation path exists to route around identity custody). Completion must be grounded in read-back durable Git and Radicle state, and the delegate signing identity must remain bound to the physical device where it was created.

Candidates considered and rejected: (1) Radicle as a third connector — retains capability registry and dispatch where no runtime choice remains; contradicts the decided removal. (2) Generic forge polymorphism preserved for hypothetical backends — the neutrality cap is precisely the cost being removed; no second live backend exists in the target program. (3) Designing WeForge or custom COBs now — stock rad cob create/update exists for external types, but no lived inadequacy justifies an object model; the program is inhabit-first. (4) GitHub/SourceHut kept as a permanent transitional layer — a prolonged dual path; history remains as evidence without live backends. (5) A 'Radicle abstraction layer' reproducing the eight-operation tool surface as a rad-flavored facade — Radicle operations are local CLI and Git acts whose results are directly inspectable; re-wrapping them recreates the translation boundary the decision removes; only boundaries earned by ownership, testability, or the security boundary may be introduced. (6) Local artifact production standing in for durable mutation — Radicle is local-first, so a created COB or pushed ref proves nothing about propagation; verification must read replicated state. (7) Inheriting groundwork#538's stub framing ('protocol state carried as signed custom COBs') — rejected as backlog anchoring: the stub predates the operator's phased decision and must be re-scoped to the stock-substrate boundary, not obeyed.

Chosen bounded exigence: replace Groundwork's collaboration surface with one Radicle-native realization — retire the vendored capability contract and all eight operation invocation points; define git+rad mechanics with durable-state verification in their place; re-home handle identity semantics; update conformance, tests, documentation, and installer accordingly; and prove removal rather than bypass. Boundary: rad enablement of the execution substrate (base image, agentd runner, node and key provisioning on babbie) and commons/runa authority or cleanup changes are named dependencies, not absorbed work; WeForge MVP, custom COBs, historical issue migration, and the canonical repository transfer are out of scope; implementation is gated on the connector-era release boundary (M1 accepted; groundwork v0.3.0 and runa v0.2.0 finals published) and on the commons Radicle-substrate ADR (commons#108) that carries the decision authority.
